title: One bite, or six: an ant fight at two settings of the arms-race reach
question: Three ants attacking one, same box, same seed, same moment. In one the defender wears the best shell an ant lineage can currently evolve and the fight is over in a single bite. In the other the shell is thicker and the same three mouths have to work at it. Which one reads as a fight rather than a deletion -- and is the slower one satisfying to watch, or just slower?
context_md:
Ant flesh resists 0.25 and an ant bites at 1.0, so on the shipped axis the best plate a lineage reaches is 0.50 and every ant is one-shot by every ant at every point on the axis. `World::trait_reach` widens the armour and jaw slots together; it ships at 1 and the box is byte-identical there.

**Read `gnaws` under each panel, not the frames.** A gnaw is a bite that failed to open a cell. The two arms are different worlds after the first tick -- armour is billed per tick, so the armoured ant burns more and therefore walks somewhere else -- so where two ants happen to meet is a different schedule in each, and this one seed has both defenders dying. **Over six seeds the outcome is 0 of 6 defenders surviving at the shipped reach against 4 of 6 at the top of the dial.**

Nothing here is on by default. This is what a lineage could evolve into if the dial is up.
